claim_evidence.anchor: Stephen McAdams, Meghan Goodchild, and Kit Soden develop a taxonomy of orchestral grouping in a 2022 article
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Bibliographic author/year, Music Theory Online 28(3), 2022; abstract and heading.

claim_evidence.anchor: Concurrent grouping concerns components that are heard together as one event
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [3.2], Example 2, concurrent grouping: event formation.

claim_evidence.anchor: Sequential grouping connects events across time into streams
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [3.2], Example 2 and [5.1], sequential grouping.

claim_evidence.anchor: Segmental grouping divides those streams into larger units
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [3.2] and [6.2], segmentation and orchestral contrasts.

claim_evidence.anchor: onset synchrony, harmonic relationships, and correlated changes as grouping cues
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [3.7] concurrent grouping; common onset, harmonicity and parallel spectral change.

claim_evidence.anchor: They do not say that unison doubling always creates a single instrument
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [4.1] specifically distinguishes blend and non-blend for coupled sound sources. Text interpretation.

claim_evidence.anchor: The taxonomy's discussion of orchestral contrasts
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [6.2] and Example 22 on timbral shifts, antiphonal contrasts and boundaries.

claim_evidence.anchor: The supplied event lists make the examples reproducible with a small offline renderer
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original text-only score and standard-library renderer in this pack, distinct from official DawDreamer API.

claim_evidence.anchor: Each bar starts with E above middle C for one beat
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original local JSON score, common foreground across all variants. This musical content is not from the cited taxonomy.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the fourth and eighth bars the final tone changes to C above middle C
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original local score bars 4/8, E4 G4 A4 C5; not a source-derived cadence.

claim_evidence.anchor: A quiet low C remains throughout all eight bars
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original lab event list; eight C2 whole-bar notes for each variant.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the second study, the reference melody is played by two differently colored synthetic voices
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original local source melody plus unison copy, guided by [4.1] doubling vocabulary.

claim_evidence.anchor: Nikolay Rimsky-Korsakov's Principles of Orchestration devotes sustained attention to doubling
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: 1922 Vol. I Chapter II doubled melodies and instruments; historic primary text.

claim_evidence.anchor: appeared in the edition edited by Maximilian Steinberg, published in 1922
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Title/editor page in Project Gutenberg, Édition Russe de Musique 1922; note unfinished manuscript origins discussed in prefatory matter.

claim_evidence.anchor: If two identical sine waves were aligned in phase
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Linear superposition of two in-phase sinusoids at equal frequency is a mathematical example, not claimed from the MTO paper.

claim_evidence.anchor: the new part lives in the same broad register as the melody
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original JSON crowded_background; explicit C4 E4 G4 E4, score observation.

claim_evidence.anchor: the identical pitch classes and rhythm are placed one octave lower
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original JSON spaced_background; exact C3 E3 G3 E3 at same note times.

claim_evidence.anchor: McAdams, Goodchild, and Soden relate perceptual organization to similarities in pitch, timbre, intensity, and temporal proximity
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [5.1] sequential grouping, with cited foundational work.

claim_evidence.anchor: Their article also cites David Huron's work on the differentiation of timbres in part writing
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [5.1], Huron (2016, pp. 114–116) attribution via paper; secondary citation, not independently checked in the Huron book.

claim_evidence.anchor: the Philharmonia Orchestra's instrument guide describes violin bowing
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Violin article, Bowing section, including up/down-bow distinctions.

claim_evidence.anchor: Its cello guide explains how bow strokes affect repeated-note accompaniments
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Cello article, Bowing section and Introduction; on-string and bouncing strokes.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the third bar, the lower arpeggiating line enters
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original staged_entrances JSON accompaniment starts beat 8, first beat of bar 3.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the fifth bar, a higher sustained line joins
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original staged_entrances JSON upper sustained E5 begins beat 16, bar 5.

claim_evidence.anchor: the first four bars of the melody use one synthetic color
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original timbral_handoff JSON, foreground sine bars 1–4 and harmonic bars 5–8.

claim_evidence.anchor: McAdams, Goodchild, and Soden call attention to timbral shifts
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: [6.2] and Example 22 distinguish timbral shifts from antiphonal/call-response contrasts.

claim_evidence.anchor: The Philharmonia's flute guide identifies middle C as the normal bottom
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Flute article, Range: C4, optional B3 on B foot, and piccolo sounds octave higher than written.

claim_evidence.anchor: A violin's strings are normally tuned G3, D4, A4, and E5
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Violin article, Range, string tunings.

claim_evidence.anchor: The cello, tuned C2, G2, D3, and A3
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Cello article, Range: open string pitches C/G/D/A; octaves are standard scientific pitch notation.

claim_evidence.anchor: The double bass usually sounds an octave below its written part
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Double bass article, Range: sounds octave lower than written; sounding string pitches E1/A1/D2/G2.

claim_evidence.anchor: The Philharmonia describes sustained inner harmonies as a common role for horns
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Horn article, Introduction, sustained inner-harmony use and powerful full-ensemble role.

claim_evidence.anchor: The trumpet guide describes both forceful projection and subtle, muted lyrical playing
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Trumpet article, Introduction, contrasting forceful/muted melodic uses.

claim_evidence.anchor: The Philharmonia's violin discussion notes that a passage at a given sounding pitch may differ
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Violin article, Range: same pitch on G versus A string yields different tonal character.

claim_evidence.anchor: its cello materials discuss sul C and sul G instructions
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Cello article, Range, specific string instruction labels.

claim_evidence.anchor: DawDreamer's official user guide describes the RenderEngine
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Official docs Overview, Basic Workflow, Rendering Audio and Graph Management.

claim_evidence.anchor: Ardour's official manual documents automation of gain and panning
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Ardour Manual: Automation bullet list and Panning overview.

claim_evidence.anchor: Source-track count, DSP cost, and perceptual density are three different quantities
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Conceptual comparison of source-track count, computational cost and perceptual grouping; synthesis not a quoted empirical result.

claim_evidence.anchor: The unison version asks whether simultaneous attacks form one composite sound
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original study; perceptual question motivated by MTO [4.1], no result claimed.

claim_evidence.anchor: The crowded and spaced versions ask how register affects the distinction between layers
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original lab contrasting registers; hypotheses, not published listener responses.

claim_evidence.anchor: The growing version asks whether entrances can articulate form
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original study, motivated by MTO grouping theory, not a source transcription.

claim_evidence.anchor: The handoff version asks whether changing a source can mark a section
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original handoff test, motivated by MTO [6.2], no guaranteed perceptual effect.

citation_policy: Claims mapped to exact audible text anchors and source locators. Source records distinguish available full text from chapter abstracts. Studies are original note-event data, not material extracted from cited compositions. Mechanical reference checks do not establish interpretive correctness.
